So, we have 10 more classes left in the lecture series. And in these 10 classes, what I'm going to do is show you how the American Empire will fall and what will replace the American Empire is Israel, or what we call Pax Judeica. For these next 10 classes, I'll provide an overview of history and demonstrate why it will lead ultimately to the Pax Judeica.

The first comment asks about restoring the right hemisphere or becoming more creative. The answer is that you have to reject materialism—reject money, power, and materialism in order to embrace your creativity and your right hemisphere. As a society, we'll need a major crisis threatening our existence to come together and be more altruistic and creative. Falling in love, having children, volunteering, helping others, and being kind and generous can activate the right hemisphere.

The second comment asks if I'm teaching only one class with three different sections. I'm only teaching one lecture series but offering it in three different sections.

The third comment inquires about my journey to find some LSD. While I have an interest in psychedelics, I don't personally use them because I believe I'm already connected to the divine through an altruistic lifestyle and don't need psychedelics to break out of this materialistic world.

A question asks if I could make a video on understanding history without bias. It's impossible to be unbiased. However, you can look at documents critically and analyze them thoroughly. The problem is often we lack documentation or have it from only one source, making unbiased analysis challenging. With this class, I'm proposing a new theory of how to understand history, which will improve your understanding of history and the world. This model has three components: understanding historical patterns, using game theory, and incorporating religious eschatology.

All cultures and individuals have a certain religious outlook found in their sacred texts like the Bible or Quran. These texts provide insight into how they perceive and want history to develop. We'll explore these strategies and adapt them for our historical understanding.
